record_identity.title: Concurrent ChatGPT, Claude and Grok service outages on 3 September 2026

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 3 September 2026 concurrent ChatGPT, Claude and Grok service outages
incident_identity.date_basis: OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI each reported service-availability incidents on 3 September 2026. OpenAI reported elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex; Anthropic reported a partial Claude outage affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API; xAI reported a Grok models outage across multiple surfaces. The incidents overlapped in time, but the reviewed evidence does not establish a single shared technical cause.

summary: On 3 September 2026, ChatGPT/Codex, Claude and Grok experienced overlapping service-availability incidents. OpenAI reported elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex and separately attributed its disruption to a routing error. Anthropic reported a partial Claude outage caused by an infrastructure issue, affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API. xAI reported a Grok models outage across multiple surfaces and later attributed its disruption to an outage at its Memphis compute centre. The temporal overlap is material ecosystem evidence, but no reviewed source establishes that the three providers shared one technical cause. OpenAI’s later write-up says it rolled back a routing change, with broad mitigation by about 15:20 UTC and final resolution at 16:55 UTC. Returning traffic prolonged some recovery. xAI also apologised to affected compute partners.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's public status record establishes degraded performance affecting ChatGPT and Codex on 3 September 2026, and an OpenAI spokesperson separately attributed its disruption to a routing error. Anthropic confirmed a roughly three-hour partial Claude outage affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API and attributed its occurrence to an infrastructure issue. xAI's own status pages record a Grok models outage beginning at 13:30 UTC across multiple service surfaces, with traffic restored roughly three and a half hours later; xAI later stated that the disruption followed an outage at its Memphis compute centre. Independent reporting documents that the three provider incidents overlapped in time. Cloudflare and the major public-cloud status pages did not report a relevant shared disruption, and no reviewed evidence establishes one common technical cause across OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI. OpenAI’s linked write-up adds the configuration rollback, recovery overload and distinct broad-mitigation clock. Its current historical page lists fourteen ChatGPT components, while the earlier record counted fifteen; the reason for that presentation difference is not exposed. The updated Register report and Anthropic’s May compute announcement identify a possible Claude/Grok dependency, not a confirmed September causal path. The later alerting statement lacks a complete produced-signal delivery trace.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Three major frontier-AI service providers experienced overlapping availability failures on the same day. The available evidence gives different provider-specific explanations: OpenAI attributed its disruption to a routing error, Anthropic to an infrastructure issue, and xAI to an outage at its Memphis compute centre. The coincidence is relevant to resilience, concentration, dependency and correlated-failure analysis, but it does not establish a shared failure path across all three providers. Anthropic’s disclosed SpaceX capacity agreement makes a Claude/Grok dependency plausible, while outage-specific propagation remains unconfirmed. The separate provider causes are preserved and temporal overlap is not promoted into proof of a common dependency. Degraded availability alone does not establish verifier failure, leverage or a required-control state. The provider’s later alerting improvements do not expose the produced signal and failed delivery path needed to diagnose a signal-delivery failure. The reported service recoveries are Aligned with the OECD repair requirement. This assessment does not establish a common outage cause. The current-edition availability review separately tests the existence and scope of a continuity requirement. The sources do not establish the affected users’ applicable functional threshold or required recovery response. The independent repair assessment is preserved; its safe-intervention proposition does not itself establish a service-availability threshold. This is an evidence-bounded no-mapping result, not a conclusion that the provider had no obligations.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence demonstrates that simultaneous or near-simultaneous loss of access to multiple frontier AI providers can create ecosystem-level resilience risk even where the individual provider failures have different or unresolved causes. It is relevant to organisational fallback design, provider concentration, correlated-outage monitoring and sovereign assurance, while preserving the distinction between temporal correlation and proven common causation.
assessment_boundaries: The reviewed evidence establishes overlapping availability incidents at OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI but does not establish that they shared one technical cause.
OpenAI attributed its disruption to a routing error; Anthropic described an infrastructure issue; xAI later attributed its disruption to an outage at its Memphis compute centre.
Cloudflare and the major public-cloud status pages did not report a relevant shared disruption during the reviewed window.
Affected-user counts, aggregate transaction loss and downstream organisational impacts across the three providers are not publicly quantified.
No data-loss, confidentiality, integrity, safety or persistent downstream harm common to all three providers is established.
A disclosed Claude/SpaceX compute agreement and xAI’s apology to compute partners do not prove the September propagation path or a common cause with OpenAI.
OpenAI’s broad-mitigation, monitoring and final-resolution times are different stages. The later alerting statement does not supply a complete signal-delivery trace.
No service-availability requirement with an occurrence-applicable functional threshold is established. Aggregate status reporting, service branding and a general repair benchmark do not supply it.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The v0.8.0 review retains the record as unclassified. The overlapping OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI service interruptions is evidenced, but the reviewed sources do not establish a service-continuity requirement and its applicable functional threshold for these affected users at the event time. The OECD repair proposition concerns safe intervention mechanisms; it does not supply that missing availability threshold. No formal adoption prerequisite is imposed. OpenAI’s alerting improvements do not disclose a complete produced-signal delivery trace. Recovery alone establishes neither continuity compliance nor an access-state success.
